ice.label: Ice curtain and glacier step

sources.says: Wilkes-Booth rated IV WI4; party climbed 'approximately four roped pitches on steeper ice' with snowfields to 70 deg between them. The entry's roped ice (P1 + two-pitch central flow) is three, so the curtain/glacier step is the fourth roped pitch. P1 (WI4) is called the crux, so the curtain is no harder than WI4. No source grades this curtain on its own.
Neighbouring Shooting Gallery (same start, shared lower ground) has ice curtains of WI4+ led on screws with belays; shows curtains here are pitched. Different route, so grade not transferred.

ice.note: Roped status is two-source; the specific grade is bounded (<= WI4), not stated. Use plain 'WI4' only if owner prefers the route grade.

ice.label: Crux

sources.says: 1996 first ascent: third step was roped, one lead pitch; belay at base on a fluke and a screw, belay above on two ice screws; 80-95 deg ice/shale. No WI grade for this step; whole route IV+ 5.9 WI5 mixed.
Crux about three-quarters up is a 100-foot pitch of near-vertical ice leading to steep runnelled snow.

ice.note: Pitch status is two-source. No source gives this step its own WI grade; the WI5 number is the route's overall grade, so the label avoids asserting WI5 for the step alone.

ice.label: Second step

sources.says: At the narrowest section are two steps: one climber led a pitch of mixed rock/ice/snow on belay, the partner then led the next step of ice. So both steps were lead pitches that year. No grades.
Route WI2-3 M5-; second step is a shorter step of rock or ice above the first (80 deg) step; 'a couple of short screws are handy for the ice section'.

ice.note: Conditions vary: Steph Abegg's spring report (stephabegg.com) set no protection in the couloir. Pitched in lean/icy years; the entry already says 'pitch it out in lean conditions' for step 1.

ice.label: Ridge 3

sources.says: West Ridge is six pitches from the notch; pitch 3 traverses the north face through mid-5th terrain to a gully; pitches 5 and 6 are mid-5th cracks; overall M5- (M5 when dry-tooled in March).

ice.note: The grade string 'mid 5th' has no 5.x / 'low 5th' / '5th class' token, so it draws as a leg; 'mid 5th class' fixes that. Rock, outside ice scope but a real roped pitch.

sources.says: Pitch 4 is class 3 ledges, pitches 5 and 6 mid-5th crack systems to the summit; alternate 5-pitch version has a belay at the top of the box gully.

ice.label: Snowfinger (crux)

sources.says: 'a 70-degree, horribly exposed snowfinger'; 'We used fixed belays to get across the snowfinger and up the slippery Class 4 summit rock'; belayed back across it on descent.
Party 'tag-teamed the final short pitches across the steep snowfinger'; rappelled off the summit and 'belayed back across the snowfinger'.

ice.note: Two independent reports belayed it. Neither mentions a picket on the snowfinger itself, so the stored 'picket' wording is unsourced; anchor kept generic. Season-dependent (soft snow may not need it).

leave.reason: First ascent soloed the two 75-degree pitches (protection available but not placed). AAJ 1996 is the only account; no source says this step is belayed. Stays a travel leg.

AAJ 1961: a 300 ft, 50-degree ice patch 'ascended' with no mention of belays or screws (only pitons on the grade III rock below). Summitpost 403. Nothing says pitched; the stored 'AI3' is the entry's own. Leave as leg.

MP gives only M5+ X Grade V and 'pins, screws, nuts, cams'; AAJ 1971 winter account has one 60-degree ice pitch near the ice cliff and no pitch grades. No source for per-step style; also a span of terrain, not a pitch. Leave.
Karakoram report: 50-60 degree headwall, anchor + belay for a snow assessment only; Mountaineers/CascadeClimbers 403. No source says ice steps are belayed. Leave as glacier travel.

MP: 40-50 ft rock/ice, screws/pickets/rock gear. AAJ 1968: front-pointing and step-cutting, one ice screw; belays not mentioned. A 2018 report of a belayed hourglass is on Ptarmigan Ridge, not here. Leave.
Grade '5th class' already matches the roped-pitch rule, so it already draws as a pitch (MP: clearing it can require 5th; AAJ: 50 ft, hard 5th).
'low 5th' already matches the pitch rule; MP lists them as rope-length ridge pitches. No change needed.
AAJ: snowfields to 70 degrees lie BETWEEN the roped ice pitches; simul/pickets. Stays a leg.

Do not change. USGS EPQS reads 4926 ft at the pin (47.4944,-121.2877), so it is the 5,000 ft valley creek, not the PCT crossing (PCT ford is the 3,400 ft pin at 5.5 mi). Route text: 6 mi to the PCT crossing, then 1-2 mi off-trail to the 3,600 ft camp, then on to 5,000 ft, so about 9 mi is consistent, and the summitpost '20 mi round trip' agrees (the entry's '16 miles' disagrees with its own pins). 6.5 is barely above the 6.3 mi straight line and would be too small. Optionally rename the pin 'Upper Lemah Creek (5,000 ft)'.
